novelty.justification: The claim’s intended novelty route is mechanistic—“instruction/RLHF tuning improves reasoning primarily by reweighting and gating pre-existing pretraining circuits … rather than by constructing new computation”—rather than merely a new application setting. Searches for “instruction tuning circuit reuse pretraining circuits,” “fine-tuning enhances existing mechanisms circuit analysis,” and “RLHF reweights existing circuits gating” identify the closest work as the ICML 2025 paper “Towards Understanding Fine-Tuning Mechanisms of LLMs via Circuit Analysis,” which already compares circuits before and after fine-tuning and reports high node similarity with substantial edge changes; Prakash et al.’s 2024 entity-tracking study likewise argues that fine-tuning enhances existing mechanisms. Moving from those results to instruction/RLHF-tuned reasoning models and predicting concentration in “a few gating components” is a natural extension and somewhat sharper operationalization, but the central old-circuits-versus-new-circuits relationship is already established rather than a new core insight.
